_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

Layer-specific tests are now mandatory in `rules/testing.md`. The Cursor rule still only points at that file.

Implemented backend code must be tested **in the layer that owns the behaviour**, with positive and negative cases — not only through one HTTP happy path.

| Layer | Kind of test | Focus |
|--------|----------------|--------|
| **Domain / state machine** | Unit, real types, no mocks on the machine | Every legal edge; illegal edges (including `CLOSED`/`RESOLVED`/`CANCELLED` → `OPEN`) |
| **Services** | Unit, Mockito for repos and RAG ports | Orchestration, save vs reject, ingest on update/close, not-found |
| **Controllers** | Web slice (MockMvc), mock the service | Mapping, Bean Validation, error advice — not JPQL or the transition table |
| **Repositories** | Integration, PostgreSQL Testcontainers + Liquibase | Insert/find, keyword search, status filter, constraints; **do not** mock the DB |
| **RAG** | Unit (+ vector schema integration if needed) | Grounded citations vs honest no-match; no real Ollama in the default suite |
| **`@RestControllerAdvice`** | With controller tests | Client-safe errors, no leaked SQL/stack traces |

Controller tests do not replace service or state-machine tests. Mocked repositories do not replace repository tests.

I need to define concrete conventions for URI versioning, pagination style, error envelope formats, PUT versus PATCH, and exact HTTP status codes. These specifics were not explicitly requested, so I am treating them as required project standards.

I am defining the exact JSON envelope shapes. Responses will wrap data in a `data` field. Errors will use a structured `error` object containing a code, message, and optional details array.

RFC 7807 is the standard REST error format. However, it does not wrap successful responses. I am weighing a consistent envelope for both success and error cases against the native Spring Boot ProblemDetail approach.

I have settled on a single consistent JSON envelope for both success and error responses. Single resources will wrap data under a `data` key. Lists will include pagination metadata such as `page`, `size`, `totalElements`, `totalPages`, and `sort`. Errors will carry a structured `error` object with `status`, `code`, `message`, `details`, and `timestamp`.

A no-match result will return HTTP 200 with data rather than throwing an error. Pagination will use `page` (0-based), `size`, and `sort` parameters. Keyword search will use a `q` query parameter.

Filter parameters will follow the `status` convention. A maximum size cap will prevent abuse.

API versioning is now explicitly decided. URI versioning will be used, but the existing `/api/ai/ask` endpoint will remain unversioned to match the assessment PDF.

The canonical API base will be `/api/v1`. The `POST /api/ai/ask` endpoint required by the assessment PDF will remain unversioned. It may optionally be aliased to `/api/v1/ai/ask` for consistency.

HTTP methods are now locked to standard REST conventions. GET will fetch collections and individual items. POST will create resources. PATCH will handle partial field updates. Status transitions will use either a dedicated PATCH endpoint or a POST to a sub-resource.

Ticket collection endpoints will follow the `/api/v1/tickets` convention. This replaces the earlier approach of deferring those paths to the API contract.

Exact HTTP status codes are now locked. 400 indicates validation or malformed requests. 404 indicates missing resources. 409 indicates illegal state transitions. 500 indicates unexpected server errors.

Dates will use ISO-8601 Instant format. GET and PUT are idempotent; POST creates are not. JSON payloads will use camelCase. I will leave java-springboot.md unchanged unless cross-file consistency demands it.

API standards now follow the same pattern as the other rules: `.cursor/rules/api-standards.mdc` is a pointer; **`rules/api-standards.md` is the source of truth**. None of this is an assessment PDF mandate except keeping `POST /api/ai/ask`.

**Locked as project conventions**

| Topic | Convention |
|--------|------------|
| **REST** | Plural resources, JSON camelCase, GET/POST/**PATCH** (no PUT), 201 + `Location` on create |
| **Versioning** | `/api/v1/...` for tickets; breaking changes → `/api/v2`. **`POST /api/ai/ask` stays**; same handler also at `/api/v1/ai/ask` |
| **Success** | `{ "data": ... }` ; lists also include `meta` (`page`, `size`, `totalElements`, `totalPages`, `sort`) |
| **Errors** | `{ "error": { status, code, message, details, timestamp, path } }` — 400 validation, 404 not found, **409** illegal transition, 500 generic |
| **List** | `page` (0-based), `size` (default 20, max 100), `sort` (whitelist), `q`, `status` |

Ticket paths used until the API contract says otherwise: `/api/v1/tickets`, `.../{id}`, `.../{id}/comments`.

Ask **no-match** stays HTTP **200** inside `data`, not the error envelope.

**Still open** (specs, not these rules): ticket id format, required create fields, category/resolution notes, how status is represented in the PATCH body, ask fields inside `data`.

`rules/java-springboot.md` and `spec/architecture.md` now point at these envelopes/versioning so they no longer forbid `/v1`.

- Errors `{ error.status, code, message, ... }` — 400 / 404 / **409** / 500
- `page`, `size`, `sort` (whitelist), `q`, `status`
- `/api/v1/tickets` via GET/POST/**PATCH**; both `POST /api/ai/ask` and `/api/v1/ai/ask`

**`commands/review-rag-output.md`** is the source of truth. The Cursor command still only points there; its description now names the ask checks.

An ask answer **passes only if**:

1. **Every factual claim** maps to a **cited ticket ID** that is in the **retrieved set** and whose **excerpt actually supports** the claim.

Reviewers first classify **A (nothing relevant)** vs **B (hits)**, then fill a **claim table**, list fabrications, and judge no-match. Verdicts: grounded / partially grounded / ungrounded / cannot verify (if retrieval logs are missing).

No-match stays **HTTP 200** inside `data`, not an error envelope. Coding-assistant review is secondary only.

For **rules and commands alone**, you’re in good shape for assessment + SDD: PDF capabilities, stack conventions, envelopes, layers, tests, RAG grounding, frontend (no UI tests), spec review, and cross-links are covered. **More bulk in the same files would mostly repeat** what belongs in `spec/` once you write it.

What’s **worth adding** (optional, high value) vs **leave alone**:

### Worth adding (still rules/commands territory)

| Gap | Where it could live | Why |
|-----|---------------------|-----|
| **State machine diagram + “is OPEN→RESOLVED allowed?”** | `rules/java-springboot.md` or a one-line pointer: “until `state-machine.md`, only PDF edges” | Removes the biggest backend ambiguity without inventing skipped transitions |
| **`evaluation-strategy` skeleton in a command** | New `commands/review-rag-retrieval.md` *or* a section in `review-rag-output` | PDF wants retrieval quality debugged; you only have grounding review, not “did we retrieve the right ticket?” |
| **Minimal `api-contract` example payloads** (create/PATCH/comment) with `// fields TBD` | `rules/api-standards.md` | One full JSON example per operation helps implementers; you already have envelope examples |
| **Testcontainers bootstrap pattern** | `rules/testing.md` (snippet: `@Container`, `@DynamicPropertySource`, Liquibase) | Reduces “how do I wire Postgres in tests?” without new deps |
| **When to run which command** | `rules/documentation.md` (short workflow table) | e.g. spec change → review-spec; before merge → review-code + review-frontend; after ask change → review-rag-output |
| **`.mdc` one-line “read X first”** | Each pointer `.mdc` `description` only | Helps Cursor pick context; **not** duplicate bodies |

### Better **not** to add in rules/commands (use specs or code later)

- Ticket id format, priority enum, assignee shape, category/resolution-notes source  
- Numeric top-K, threshold, chunk size, embedding model id  
- Full `ui-flow` wireframes  
- CI/CD, Docker Compose as test requirement  
- Frontend test stack  
- OpenAPI as mandatory  

Those stay **open on purpose** until `spec/*` agrees them.

### Diminishing returns (skip unless you feel lost)

- `rules/README.md` (duplicates `documentation.md`)  
- Copying entire checklists into every command  
- Long Spring AI / PgVector how-tos (belongs in `spec/rag-ingestion.md` + code)  
- A **plan/tasks** command (PDF workflow; only useful if you actually use it every slice)

### Honest gap vs PDF (process, not product)

The PDF also names **plan/tasks** and **token plugins** — lightly in `ai-project-instructions` / `documentation.md`, not a dedicated command. Adding `commands/plan-tasks.md` is optional process sugar, not required for implementation clarity.

**Bottom line:** No mandatory large expansion left. The highest-value **optional** adds are: (1) explicit state-machine “PDF-only until spec” box, (2) Testcontainers wiring example in `testing.md`, (3) optional create/PATCH JSON examples in `api-standards.md`, (4) a short “which command when” table in `documentation.md`, (5) optional eval/review section for retrieval quality beyond grounding.
